paper_type_rationale: The paper proposes DeepEyes, an end-to-end RL-trained multimodal model that learns interleaved multimodal chain-of-thought and active perception without cold-start supervised reasoning data.
dominant_domain: Vision-language reasoning, active perception, reinforcement learning, tool use, high-resolution visual reasoning.
must_cover: DeepEyes learns to think with images through iMCoT and active perception.
The model decides whether to answer or zoom into image regions after textual reasoning steps.
Training uses GRPO with answer, format, and conditional tool reward.
The data curation strategy combines V* visual search, ArxivQA chart data, and ThinkLite-VL reasoning data.
Main results improve high-resolution perception, MME-RealWorld-Lite, grounding, hallucination, and reasoning benchmarks.
Training dynamics show a progression from exploration to efficient visual exploitation.
key_numbers: On V* Overall, DeepEyes reaches 90.1 versus 71.2 for Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
On HR-Bench 8K Overall, DeepEyes reaches 72.6 versus 65.3 for Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
On MME-RealWorld-Lite Overall, DeepEyes reaches 53.2 versus 42.3 for Qwen2.5-VL.
On MathVista, DeepEyes reaches 70.1 versus 68.3 for the reproduced Qwen2.5-VL baseline.
Conditional tool reward reaches V* 90.1, HR-4K 75.1, and HR-8K 72.6.
Without tool reward, results are V* 87.4, HR-4K 53.4, and HR-8K 55.4.
DeepEyes-32B reaches V* 93.3 and WeMath 55.9, with IoU 0.53.
iMCoT reaches HR-8K 72.6, while RL with text-only CoT reaches 60.8.
real_comparisons: Compared with workflow-based methods, DeepEyes does not require manually defined active perception workflows.
Compared with cold-start SFT methods, DeepEyes learns active perception through end-to-end RL.
Compared with text-only RL, iMCoT improves ultra-high-resolution reasoning by inserting cropped visual observations.
Compared with PatchCue and MINT-CoT, DeepEyes relies less on explicit cue supervision and more on reward-induced behavior.

central_claims.claim: End-to-end RL can elicit active perception without cold-start SFT.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: DeepEyes is trained with GRPO and achieves strong results while learning to trigger zoom-in actions.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove that all tool-use behaviors can emerge without cold-start data.

central_claims.claim: Conditional tool reward is important for useful active perception.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: The ablation shows conditional reward outperforms both no tool reward and unconditional reward on high-resolution benchmarks.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not show whether a denser process reward would be better than this sparse conditional reward.

central_claims.claim: Interleaved visual perception matters most for high-resolution tasks.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: The gap between iMCoT and text-only RL is largest on HR-8K, where fine visual detail matters.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not establish that zoom-in is the best possible visual operation.

claim_boundaries: The main tool is crop or zoom-in; richer tools are only tested lightly through a rotate prompt.
The primary base model is Qwen2.5-VL-7B, with limited larger-scale evidence.
The method still has localization failures and reasoning shortcuts.
The training data is curated for active perception utility.
negative_or_limiting_results: Without tool reward, HR-4K falls to 53.4 and HR-8K falls to 55.4.
Text-only RL reaches only 60.8 on HR-8K, far below iMCoT.
POPE adversarial decreases from 85.9 to 84.0 in the reproduced comparison.
The limitations section reports insufficient reasoning richness and inaccurate target localization.
mechanism_result_map: Conditional tool reward maps to sustained useful active perception.
Difficulty and perception-utility filtering maps to better initial RL sampling without SFT.
iMCoT state formulation maps to interleaving text tokens and image observation tokens.
Scaling challenging reasoning data maps to simultaneous gains in V*, MathVerse, and WeMath.
Adding rotate through prompt maps to HR-OCR-Rot improvement without retraining.
comparative_positioning: DeepEyes is a Train-line active perception method, distinct from training-free visual refocusing methods such as VisRef.
Compared with PatchCue, it does not train explicit patch cue outputs.
Compared with MINT-CoT, it does not rely on step-token supervised visual alignment.
Compared with DeepEyesV2, it is narrower but cleaner as a study of active perception emergence.
reuse_takeaways: For 3D agents, reward visual actions only when they lead to correct answers, not merely when tools are called.
A perception-utility filter is useful for selecting examples where visual action can change the result.
Training dynamics should track tool count, response length, grounding IoU, and task score together.
Text-only RL can learn reasoning style but may fail when details require visual revisiting.
followup_questions: Would a dense localization reward improve over the sparse conditional tool reward?
Can active perception extend from crop to multi-view rendering in 3D scenes?
How sensitive is DeepEyes to the quality of the perception-utility filter?
Does the model truly use cropped observations under counterfactual crop replacement?

section_plan.focus: Explain why VLMs need active visual revisiting during reasoning rather than only text-based CoT.
Describe V* visual search, ArxivQA chart data, ThinkLite-VL reasoning data, and perception-utility filtering.
Cover iMCoT rollout state, zoom-in observations, GRPO, and conditional tool reward.
Report high-resolution, MME-RealWorld, grounding, reasoning, tool reward, scaling, and iMCoT ablations.
Interpret the three-stage training dynamics and hallucination mitigation mechanism through active perception.
Record limited tool scope, localization errors, reasoning shortcuts, and dependence on foundation model capability.
